title.en: Six Miles of Walking, One Mile of Progress

dek.zh: 船被浮冰压毁后，沙克尔顿带队在冰上分批搬运、艰难行进，苦干四天之后决定在一块厚浮冰上扎营等待。他自己写下了理由：雪面太软走不远，而附近可能开出水道。
dek.en: After the pack ice crushed their ship, Shackleton's party struggled across the floes, ferrying loads in relays; after four days of hard effort he decided to camp on a thick floe and wait. He wrote down his reasons: the snow was too soft to get far, and leads might open close by.

paras.zh: 探险队由沙克尔顿率领。南极的浮冰上，他的船被冰压得扶正无望，只能放弃。人还活着，食品和装备也还在。他写下新的任务，只有一句：任务是让全体队员抵达陆地。
paras.en: Shackleton led the expedition. On the Antarctic pack ice, his ship was crushed by the ice beyond all hope of ever being righted, and the men had to abandon her. They were alive and well, and their stores and equipment were still in hand. He set down the new task in a single sentence: "The task is to reach land with all the members of the Expedition."

paras.zh: 可怎么到陆地？冰面是松软的湿雪，装备要分批来回搬运，一天下来直线只前进约一英里。苦干四天之后的第二天早上，他决定停下来扎营。
paras.en: But how to reach land? The surface was loose, wet snow, and loads had to be ferried back and forth in relays; a day's march gained about a mile in a straight line. On the morning after four days of hard effort, he decided to stop and camp.

heading.en: The Original Plan, and the Two-Pound Rule

paras.zh: 原计划要宏大得多：若能按时登陆，横穿队伍就立刻出发，踏上1800英里的行程，希望在五个月内穿越极点，抵达罗斯海一侧的基地；若登陆太晚，就先越冬，在秋季和次年春季布置补给站，1915年尽早出发。船被压毁之后，任务换成了另一件事——让全队上岸。
paras.en: The plan he began with was far grander. If the landing was made in time, "the Transcontinental party will set out on their 1800-mile journey at once," he wrote, "in the hope of accomplishing the march across the Pole and reaching the Ross Sea base in five months." Should the landing be made too late in the season, the party would go into winter quarters, lay out depots during the autumn and the following spring, and set out as early as possible in 1915. Once the ice had crushed the ship, the task became something else entirely: get the whole party onto land.

paras.zh: 船被冰困了281天，随浮冰向西北漂了570多英里。弃船时他算过他们的处境：离保利特岛还有346英里，那是最近一处可能找到食物和住处的地方。岛上有一座1902年瑞典探险队盖的小屋，里面存着阿根廷救援船留下的物资；这批物资他再熟悉不过，正是他当年在伦敦替阿根廷政府采购的。向西最近的冰障约180英里，可到了那里，离保利特岛仍有约360英里，而冰障上没有任何活命的办法。
paras.en: The ship had been locked in the ice for 281 days and had drifted more than 570 miles to the north-west. When they left her he worked out where they stood. They were 346 miles from Paulet Island, "the nearest point where there is any possibility of finding food and shelter." A small hut built there by the Swedish expedition in 1902 held stores left by the Argentine relief ship, and he knew those stores well: he had bought them himself in London on behalf of the Argentine Government. The nearest barrier to the west was about 180 miles away, but a party going there would still be about 360 miles from Paulet Island, and "there would be no means of sustaining life on the barrier."

heading.en: From Dump Camp to Ocean Camp

paras.zh: 在被他们称为抛弃营的地方，装备经历了一次大幅筛选。他决定给每人发一整套全新的 Burberrys 和内衣，再加新袜子；他还定下规矩：个人物品不得超过两磅，除了最必需的东西，一律不上路。照他的说法，他们负担不起多余的重量。
paras.en: At a place they named Dump Camp, the equipment went through a severe weeding-out. He decided to issue each man a complete new set of Burberrys and underclothing, along with a supply of new socks. He also fixed the rule: "personal gear must not exceed two pounds per man," which meant nothing but bare necessaries would go on the march. As he put it, they could not afford to cumber themselves with unnecessary weight.

paras.zh: 于是有了那个读完忘不掉的细节：金币被扔掉，照片被留下。亚历山德拉王后赠给船一本圣经，里面有她的亲笔字迹；他从这本圣经上撕下了扉页，还撕下了约伯记中的一页。
paras.en: And so the detail that stays with you: "sovereigns were thrown away and photographs were kept." Queen Alexandra had given the ship a Bible with her own writing in it. He tore the fly-leaf out of it, and also a page of Job.

paras.zh: 真正压人的是船。两条小艇连同装备和底下的雪橇，每条都超过一吨。他写道，雪橇是最薄弱的一环：载着这样的重量走在粗糙的压力冰上，几乎不可能不被压碎，而前面这样的冰面大概还有300英里。
paras.en: The real weight was the boats. Each of them, with its gear and the sledges beneath it, weighed more than a ton. "The sledges were the point of weakness." It seemed almost hopeless, he wrote, to keep them from smashing under their loads on rough pressure-ice "which stretched ahead of us for probably 300 miles."

paras.zh: 第一天的走法是接力。开路的小队拿着镐和铲，在冰脊间为拉船的雪橇凿出一条路；七组狗队把雪橇往前拉半英里，再折回去拉其余的雪橇；沃斯利管着两条船，十五个人拉，也得分段倒运。他们跨过两道正在张开的冰缝，缝里有虎鲸探出头来。到下午5点，他们向北西北方向走了一英里。
paras.en: The first day's method was the relay. A pioneer party with picks and shovels broke a road through the pressure-ridges for the sledges carrying the boats. The seven dog teams "took their sledges forward for half a mile, then went back for the other sledges." Worsley took charge of the two boats, "with fifteen men hauling, and these also had to be relayed." They crossed two opening cracks with killer whales pushing their snouts through, and by 5 p.m. they had covered a mile, north-north-west.

paras.zh: 行军的账很难看。头几天里有一天，直线只前进了约一英里；为了绕开障碍，实际走过的距离至少两英里；分批搬运、来回接力，又把当天走过的路程推到了六英里，有几组狗队至少跑了十英里。那晚的营地扎在平坦但又年轻又咸的冰上。行军第一夜，虎鲸一直在喷气，凌晨2点，离营地约20英尺处裂开一道缝。他写道，脚下的冰薄得足以让虎鲸撞破，可近处没有别的地方能扎营，只好冒这个险。
paras.en: The arithmetic of the march made ugly reading. On one of the first days they gained about one mile in a direct line; the detours made the ground actually covered at least two miles, and the relays pushed the day's marching up to six. Some of the dog teams had covered at least ten miles. That night they camped on flat ice that "proved to be young and salty." On the first night of the march, killer whales blew all night, and at 2 a.m. a crack opened about 20 feet from the camp. The ice was thin enough for the killers to break through, he wrote, "but there was no other camping-ground within our reach and we had to take the risk."

paras.zh: 第二天早上雪下得极大，几十码外就看不清。他决定不拔营：在破碎的浮冰上很难找到路，把船弄进危险的位置可能酿成大祸。有人折回抛弃营取木头和鲸脂生火；天晴一些后，他和沃斯利往西探路，找到一块大浮冰，至少还能再往西北走一英里。午饭后，他们拔营继续。
paras.en: The next morning "the snow was falling so heavily that we could not see more than a few score yards ahead, and I decided not to strike camp. A path over the shattered floes would be hard to find, and to get the boats into a position of peril might be disastrous." Men went back to Dump Camp for wood and blubber for the fire. When the weather cleared a little, he and Worsley went prospecting to the west and found a large floe that offered a fairly good road for at least another mile to the north-west. After lunch they struck camp.

paras.zh: 开路时有过顺利的时候。两组狗拉着小艇出发，只需帮一次手；他写道，十四条狗干得和十八个人一样好，甚至更好。十二个人用镐和铲，十分钟就能在一道约14英尺高的冰脊上凿出一条还算平整的路。
paras.en: At one stage the work went well. Two dog teams were hitched to the cutter and "started off in splendid style. They needed to be helped only once; indeed fourteen dogs did as well or even better than eighteen men." A dozen men with picks and shovels could cut a road through a ridge about 14 feet high in ten minutes and leave a smooth, or comparatively smooth, path behind them.

paras.zh: 可总账没有变。湿雪很深，又要不断停下来凿路，他们向目标走了将近一英里，倒运和绕路又让实际路程接近六英里。看到大家都已筋疲力尽，他下令在两条船的背风处搭帐篷。搭帐篷时，一名水手在一条船里的帆布上发现一小洼雪水，每人只够抿一口；他引了一位队员日记里的话：喝过更干净的水，但很少有来得这么是时候的。
paras.en: The overall account did not change. Through wet, deep snow, with constant halts to cut a road, they "managed to march the best part of a mile towards our goal, though the relays and the deviations again made the actual distance travelled nearer six miles." Seeing that the men were all exhausted, he had the tents pitched in the lee of the two boats. While they were at it, a sailor found a little pool of thawed snow on a sail lying in one of the boats: just a sip each. He quoted what one man wrote in his diary: "One has seen and tasted cleaner, but seldom more opportunely found water."

paras.zh: 苦干四天之后的第二天，天冷而平静，还是那种湿雪。他看清，以眼下松软的雪面，加上四天苦干换来的那点成果，走不了多远；他同时也考虑到，附近有可能开出水道，那样就能划船向西北方向去找陆地。两方面的考虑合起来指向同一个决定——找一块更结实的浮冰扎营，等条件更有利时再做第二次挣脱冰牢的尝试。
paras.en: The next day, after four days of hard effort, broke cold and still, with the same wet snow. In the clearing light he could see the situation plainly. With the surface as loose as it was, and given how little they had to show for four days of strenuous effort, they would never get any great distance. And there was a second possibility to weigh: leads might open close to them, which would let them row north-west to where they might find land. The two considerations pointed one way. He decided to find a more solid floe, camp there, and stay until conditions were more favourable for a second attempt to escape from their icy prison.

paras.zh: 他们把帐篷和全部家当搬到一块又厚又重的老浮冰上，距沉船约一英里半，在那里扎下营，取名海洋营。
paras.en: Tents and everything else were moved to a thick, heavy old floe about one and a half miles from the wreck, and there they made their camp. They called it Ocean Camp.

paras.zh: 他还记下过一次挪动两条船的艰难。雪面糟透了，他们从没见过这样的冰面：人有时陷到齐臀深，到处的雪都有两英尺厚。
paras.en: He also recorded how hard it once was to shift the two boats. The surface was terrible, like nothing any of them had seen before: "We were sinking at times up to our hips, and everywhere the snow was two feet deep."

paras.zh: 他还决定尽量省下宝贵的雪橇口粮，留给那趟必然要来的小艇航行，平时几乎全靠海豹和企鹅过活。他派人回抛弃营搜罗衣物、烟草之类，可几天大雪，加上融化下陷，留在那里的许多东西已经不见了。
paras.en: He also decided, in his words, "to conserve our valuable sledging rations, which would be so necessary for the inevitable boat journey, as much as possible, and to subsist almost entirely on seals and penguins." A party went back to Dump Camp for clothing, tobacco and whatever else they could find, but heavy snow and the thaw had swallowed a good many of the things left there.

paras.zh: 这块浮冰起初约一英里见方，后来越裂越小，成了他们将近两个月的家。两个月里，他们常回到沉船附近，捞回许多衣物、食物，还有少数私人物品。他写道，那些东西当初是怀着轻松的乐观，以为可以一路冲过移动的冰面奔向安全，才打算丢在几英里之外的。
paras.en: This floating lump of ice, about a mile square at first and later splitting into smaller and smaller pieces, was their home for nearly two months. In that time they went back again and again to the wreck and retrieved clothing, food "and some few articles of personal value which in our light-hearted optimism we had thought to leave miles behind us on our dash across the moving ice to safety."

paras.zh: 后来他们真的做了第二次尝试。途中一度因前方冰面无法通行，只好后撤半英里，换到更结实的浮冰上扎营，全队大失所望。行军七天，直线只前进了七英里半；照这个速度，要三百多天才能到西边的陆地，而食物只够四十二天，只好再次在浮冰上扎营。新的营地叫耐心营，他们在那里住了将近三个半月。
paras.en: Later they did make that second attempt. At one point the ice ahead proved impassable, and, to the intense disappointment of all, they had to retreat half a mile to get onto a stronger floe and camp. They marched for seven days and gained seven and a half miles in a direct line; at that rate it would take over three hundred days to reach the land to the west, and they had food for only forty-two days. So they camped once more on the floe. They called the new camp Patience Camp and lived there for nearly three and a half months.

heading.zh: 把停止写成有下一步的动作
heading.en: Making a Stop That Carries a Next Step

paras.zh: 一种解释是（作者推断），海洋营不是他第一次决定停下。行军第二天早上，雪大得看不清路，他就决定不拔营；天晴一些后探到一块好走的浮冰，午饭后又继续走。两次决定都在衡量眼前的路还能不能走下去。扎营等待也不是新想法：在海洋营之前，他已经写下过在最近的厚浮冰上扎营、等浮冰外漂到开阔水面的方案，并说这样还能减少冰面在脚下开裂的危险。他写道，在他们的“第一个营地”，冰面曾一夜裂开两次。从他的记述看，那是扎在船旁的营地：帐篷搭好后约晚7点，脚下的冰开裂，营地被迫挪到船头外约200码处一块更大的浮冰上；午夜又有一道裂缝穿过营地。这发生在行军开始之前，与行军第一夜那道离营地约20英尺的裂缝不是一回事。但他确信应当先尝试行军，还特别提到这个问题有心理层面的考虑：让大家觉得自己正在朝陆地走，比坐等漂流要好。海洋营是在四天苦干之后回到这个先前暂且搁置、留作退路的方案。营地选在更结实的浮冰上，理由里挂着一个具体的指望：附近可能开出水道，那时可以划船去找陆地。等条件更有利，再做第二次尝试。
paras.en: One reading, and it is the author's, is that Ocean Camp was not the first time he chose to stop. On the march's second morning, with snow too thick to see a path, he decided not to strike camp; when it cleared and a good floe turned up, they moved on after lunch. Both decisions turned on whether the way ahead could be made. Nor was camping to wait a new idea. Before Ocean Camp he had already written down the option of camping on the nearest heavy floe and awaiting the outward drift of the pack to open water, noting that it would also lessen the peril of the ice splitting under them. He wrote that at their "first camp" the ice had split twice in one night. His narrative indicates that this was the camp beside the ship: at about 7 p.m., after the tents were up, the ice split beneath them and the camp had to move to a bigger floe about 200 yards away, just beyond the bow of the ship; at midnight a crack ran right through the camp. That was before the march began, and it is not the same as the crack about 20 feet from the camp on the march's first night. But he felt sure it was right to attempt a march first, noting that there was a psychological aspect too: the men would be better off feeling they were on their way to land than simply sitting and waiting for the drift. Ocean Camp, after four days of hard effort, was a return to that option he had set aside. The camp went onto a more solid floe, and the reasoning carried a specific hope: leads opening nearby, boats in the water, land to the north-west. A second attempt was to follow once conditions improved.

paras.zh: 还有一处值得注意（作者的解读）：停下之后，他们反而能一趟趟回到沉船附近，捞回衣物、食物和少数私人物品；沙克尔顿后来说，那些私人物品当初是怀着“轻松的乐观”，才打算在冲过移动冰面奔向安全时丢在几英里之外的。他还决定让大家几乎全靠海豹和企鹅过活，把雪橇口粮留给后面的小艇航行。作者认为，停下不只是不再消耗，也是把资源重新收拢的时间。
paras.en: One more thing is worth noticing, and again it is the author's reading. Once they stopped, they could go back to the wreck again and again and retrieve clothing, food and some few articles of personal value; Shackleton later said it was in "light-hearted optimism" that they had thought to leave those articles miles behind on their dash across the moving ice to safety. He also decided they would live almost entirely on seals and penguins so that the sledging rations could be kept for the boat journey ahead. On this reading, stopping was not only a halt to the drain; it was time to gather their resources again.

paras.zh: 另一种解释是关于取舍的标准（作者推断）：金币被扔掉、照片被留下，他其实写了理由。他说自己对每人两磅的限额本就有些舍不得，因为极想把重量压到最低，但有些个人物品确实可以算作不可或缺：旅程可能很长，到另一头还可能要在荒凉的海岸上临时越冬，人在这种处境下需要有东西占住思绪，需要一件能想起远在海外的家乡和亲人的实物。他还撕下了圣经的扉页和约伯记中的一页。作者的理解是：那道上限筛的不只是重量；在冰上，金币换不来什么，照片却能让人想起家。
paras.en: A second reading, and it is the author's, concerns the standard behind the choices. The sovereigns were thrown away and the photographs were kept, and he did give his reasons. He admits he rather grudged the two-pound allowance per man, so anxious was he to keep weights down, but some personal belongings could fairly be regarded as indispensable: the journey might be a long one, and there might be a winter in improvised quarters on an inhospitable coast at the other end. In his words, "A man under such conditions needs something to occupy his thoughts, some tangible memento of his home and people beyond the seas." He also tore out the Bible's fly-leaf and a page of Job. The author's understanding is that the limit screened for more than weight: on the ice the gold coins could buy nothing, while the photographs could bring home to mind.

paras.zh: 作者提出的替代选择：比如把队伍分成两支，一支维持最低限度的探路，一支守营保存体力；或者先派少数人轻装去试水道。这类做法都要把队伍拆开。列在这里只是想说明，那天的决定不是唯一的可能，却和当时手里的条件对得上。
paras.en: Then there are alternatives the author raises for the sake of argument. The party could have been split in two, one half keeping up a minimal reconnaissance while the other held the camp and conserved its strength. Or a few men might have gone ahead lightly loaded, to feel out the leads. Both would have meant splitting the party. They are listed here only to show that the decision of that day was not the only possibility, though it did match the conditions in front of them.

paras.zh: 场景一：一个创业团队的融资没谈成，原计划已经不成立。负责人第一次全员会上最有用的，也许就是像本文开头那个一句话的新任务一样，用一句话说清新的目标：现在要做到什么，怎么算做到。
paras.en: Scenario one: a start-up's fundraising has fallen through and the original plan no longer stands. At the first all-hands meeting, the most useful thing the founder can do may be what the new task at the start of this piece did: state the new goal in one sentence, what has to be achieved now and how you will know.

paras.zh: 场景二：个人创作。连续投稿，退稿的间隙越来越长，你开始怀疑该不该每天硬写凑数。此时可以先做那次两磅的筛选：留下真正必需的（读、记、改），扔掉看起来体面但拖慢你的部分；然后给等待定一个复查日，比如两个月后看一次信号再决定。停下来不等于停笔，只是不再用六份力气换一份进度。
paras.en: Scenario two: creative work of your own. You have been submitting steadily, the gaps between rejections keep stretching, and you have begun to wonder whether forcing out words every day is worth it. This is the moment for the two-pound sort. Keep what is genuinely necessary — reading, notes, revision. Drop what looks respectable but only slows you down. Then give the waiting a review date: in two months, you check the signals and decide again. Stopping does not mean putting down the pen. It means no longer trading six measures of effort for one measure of progress.

paras.zh: 本篇的全部过程都出自沙克尔顿本人的叙述（这里用的是1920年印本的 OCR 文本），是当事人、领导者的记述。没有取得其他队员的日记作对照。他的叙述写到了队员的状态：大家筋疲力尽；第二次尝试受挫、被迫后撤时，全队大失所望；部分人似乎一度消沉，随即恢复。这些也都出自他的叙述。但营地里其他人是否同意海洋营的决定，证据里没有，本篇也不另替他们猜测心理。文中那句“喝过更干净的水”出自一位未具名队员的日记，是经沙克尔顿转引的。
paras.en: Everything in this piece comes from Shackleton's own narrative, read here through the OCR text of the 1920 printing: the account of a participant who led the party. No other member's diary has been brought in for comparison. His narrative does report the men's state: they were all exhausted; at the second setback, when they had to retreat, there was intense disappointment among all of them; and an apathy that seemed to take hold of some of the men soon passed. These reports, too, come from his narrative. Whether anyone else in the camp agreed with the Ocean Camp decision is not in the evidence, and this piece does not put further feelings in their mouths. The line about the sip of water comes from an unnamed member's diary, as quoted by Shackleton.

paras.zh: 文本是 OCR，有讹字，引用只取清晰片段，个别有讹字的词不加引号照抄。主要数字——1800英里、281天、346英里、两磅、一吨、一英里、六英里、一英里半、两个月、三个半月——都出自他的记述，未与别的记录核对。本篇也不写耐心营之后的经过，那部分不在这份证据包的覆盖范围内。
paras.en: The text is machine-read, and it carries errors. Quotations are taken only from clean stretches; a few damaged words are reproduced without quotation marks. The main figures — 1,800 miles, 281 days, 346 miles, two pounds, a ton, one mile, six miles, one and a half miles, two months, three and a half months — come from his account and have not been checked against any other record. Nor does this piece tell what happened after Patience Camp; that falls outside the evidence gathered here.

scenario.zh: 你带一个小团队做有交付期的项目，投入连续几周增加，关键指标却只挪很小一段；与此同时，一个外部条件（合作方窗口、季节、审批）可能在一两个月内变好。继续加人硬推，还是收拢资源，等窗口成熟再做第二次冲刺？
scenario.en: You lead a small team on a project with a delivery deadline. Weeks of rising input have moved the key metric by only a little. At the same time, an external condition — a partner's window, a season, an approval — may improve within a month or two. Do you keep adding people and pushing, or gather your resources and wait for the window, then make a second, concentrated push?

question.zh: 什么信号出现时，你会把继续推进改成停下来等？你给自己定的复查日是哪一天？
question.en: What signal would tell you to turn continued effort into a deliberate wait? And what review date do you set for yourself?

assumptions.zh: 每周追加投入，但关键指标每周只前进很小一段；外部条件在未来一到两个月内有可能变好；团队的体力和预算是有限的，且分散使用会让两边都做不成。
assumptions.en: Extra effort goes in every week, but the key metric advances only a little each week. The external condition may improve within one to two months. The team's energy and budget are finite, and splitting them would leave both halves unable to finish.

steps.zh:
先做一次两磅式的筛选：把资源分成必需与可弃，给每个人的负担设上限
把真实产出分开记：直线进展算一份，绕路和来回搬运的消耗单算
若直线进展持续远低于消耗，收拢队伍到一个稳固的据点，并定下明确的复查日
条件好转时做一次集中的第二次尝试，而不是每天小步硬推
steps.en:
Run a two-pound sort first: divide resources into indispensable and disposable, and cap each person's load
Record real output separately: direct progress counts as one figure, detours and ferrying are counted as their own cost
If direct progress keeps running far below the cost, gather the team onto a firm base and set an explicit review date
When conditions improve, make one concentrated second attempt instead of grinding out small steps daily

alternative.zh: 作者提出的另一种做法：不整体停下，而是分两支，一支维持最低限度的试推，一支专门盯外部窗口。代价是人力分散，两支都可能不够用。
alternative.en: Another course the author raises: instead of stopping wholesale, split in two — one part keeps up a minimal probe while the other watches the external window. The cost is a divided workforce, and neither half may prove large enough.

uncertainty_note.zh: 全部来自沙克尔顿本人的叙述（本篇用1920年印本的 OCR 文本），是当事人、领导者的记述，没有其他队员的日记作对照；OCR 有讹字，引用只取清晰片段；文中数字均出自该记述，未经独立核对；本篇不涉及耐心营之后的经过。
uncertainty_note.en: Everything here comes from Shackleton's own narrative (this piece uses the OCR text of the 1920 printing): the account of the participant who led the party, with no other member's diary for comparison. The OCR carries errors, and quotations are drawn only from clean stretches. Every figure in the piece comes from that account and has not been independently verified. What happened after Patience Camp is not covered here.

preheader.zh: 两磅个人物品、一页圣经扉页，和一个停下来的决定。
preheader.en: Two pounds of personal gear, a torn flyleaf, and a decision to stop.

sources.citation: Ernest Shackleton, South: The Story of Shackleton's Last Expedition, 1914–1917 (1920 printing; archive.org OCR)

what.zh: 沙克尔顿本人的叙述，第四、五章写弃船与海洋营。
what.en: Shackleton's own account; chapters 4–5 cover the loss of the ship and Ocean Camp.
